3	---
4	
5	## People hub: schema and permission model
6	
7	Design doc for the Directus data model behind Layer 2 of `docs/architecture.md` (the CRM / people
8	hub), per the plan agreed on issue #69. Covers the collections, fields, and permission policies;
9	deployment and rollout are tracked in the sibling issues (#92-#95) that decompose #69.
10	
11	### Scope and non-goals
12	
13	- Models what Clubspot actually gives us: people, their guardian/emergency-contact relationships,
14	  the camp schedule (programs/sessions/classes/capacity), and registrations. No household
15	  grouping — Clubspot has no concept of a household, only per-registration guardians and emergency
16	  contacts, so that's what the schema keys off.
17	- Terminology matches Clubspot and the website: **program** (Clubspot's `Camp`), **session**
18	  (`CampSession`), **class** (`CampClass`), **registration** (`Registration`/`RegistrationCampSession`)
19	  — not "enrollment."
20	- Registration status and person contact fields get **history, not just a current value** — see
21	  [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance).
22	- Auth identity is deliberately separate from person data — see [Auth identity](#auth-identity)
23	  below.
24	- Coach and guardian **portals** (thin clients calling this API) are out of scope; this doc defines
25	  the roles/policies they'll eventually use, but nothing here provisions their logins. That's #65.
26	
27	### Collections
28	
29	**people** — one row per human known to the org: staff, coaches, guardians, participants, emergency
30	contacts. Roles aren't stored — they're derived from relationships: staff from `directus_user_id` +
31	Directus role, coach from an `event_staff` row, guardian/emergency contact from a `contacts` row,
32	participant from a `registrations` row.
33	
34	No `clubspot_id` here. Clubspot has no stable person record — each registration carries its own
35	contact data, and one real person can show up as the contact on many registrations. Deduplicating
36	and collecting those into a single `people` row (by email, most likely) is the identity-resolution
37	problem #70's sync has to solve; it isn't a field this schema can just copy in.
38	
39	| Field                     | Type                                              | Notes                               |
40	| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
41	| `id`                      | uuid                                              | primary key                         |
42	| `first_name`, `last_name` | string                                            |                                     |
43	| `email`, `phone`          | string, nullable                                  | contact info, not auth              |
44	| `date_of_birth`           | date, nullable                                    | required for minors                 |
45	| `directus_user_id`        | uuid, nullable, unique, FK -> `directus_users.id` | see [Auth identity](#auth-identity) |
46	
47	**medical_profiles** — one-to-one with `people`, kept as its own collection so its permission policy
48	can be stricter than a roster-level `people` read (allergies, medications, conditions, physician
49	contact).
50	
51	| Field                                    | Type                        | Notes                                             |
52	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
53	| `person_id`                              | uuid, PK, FK -> `people.id` | one profile per person, so `person_id` is the key |
54	| `allergies`, `medications`, `conditions` | text                        | free-form                                         |
55	| `physician_name`, `physician_phone`      | string, nullable            |                                                   |
56	
57	**contacts** — one join collection for both relationship kinds Clubspot gives us (guardian and
58	emergency contact), rather than a separate table per type, since the shape is identical. Other
59	relationship kinds, if they're ever needed, get their own dedicated table rather than growing this
60	one's `relationship_type` enum.
61	
62	Like `people`, these rows have no Clubspot id of their own to key off — Clubspot doesn't model a
63	guardian/emergency contact as a linked record, just flat strings on the participant
64	(`parentGuardianName`/`_secondary`, `emergencyContact`/`emergencyRelationship`). `contact_order`
65	is what recovers Clubspot's primary-vs-secondary guardian distinction once #70 turns those flat
66	fields into rows here.
67	
68	| Field               | Type                                   | Notes                                     |
69	| ------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
70	| `id`                | uuid                                   | primary key                               |
71	| `related_person_id` | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the minor                                 |
72	| `person_id`         | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                | the guardian or emergency contact         |
73	| `relationship_type` | enum (`guardian`, `emergency_contact`) |                                           |
74	| `contact_order`     | integer                                | call order when a minor has more than one |
75	
76	**event_staff** — coach/staff assigned to a session. This is the row that makes someone a "coach"
77	(derived, not stored on `people`) — not used to scope roster permissions yet, see
78	[Permission model](#permission-model).
79	
80	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
81	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
82	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
83	| `person_id`  | uuid, FK -> `people.id`   |             |
84	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
85	
86	**programs** — matches org/Clubspot terminology: a program is what CYC calls a `Camp` in Clubspot
87	(e.g. "Youth Camp", "LTS Weekday", "ILCA Race Team") — the thing on the website you sign up for.
88	
89	| Field              | Type                     | Notes                                                                          |
90	| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
91	| `id`               | uuid                     | primary key                                                                    |
92	| `name`             | string                   |                                                                                |
93	| `category`         | string, nullable         | Clubspot's own grouping (e.g. "Summer Camp", "Junior Racing", "Adult Sailing") |
94	| `clubspot_camp_id` | string, nullable, unique | dedup key for #70                                                              |
95	
96	**sessions** — a dated instance of a program (Clubspot's `CampSession`).
97	
98	| Field                    | Type                      | Notes             |
99	| ------------------------ | ------------------------- | ----------------- |
100	| `id`                     | uuid                      | primary key       |
101	| `program_id`             | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` |                   |
102	| `start_date`, `end_date` | date                      |                   |
103	| `clubspot_session_id`    | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70 |
104	
105	**classes** — an age/skill subdivision within a program (Clubspot's `CampClass`, e.g. "Beginner" vs.
106	"Advanced"). A registration is for a specific session _and_ class — see `registrations` below.
107	
108	| Field               | Type                      | Notes                                                                  |
109	| ------------------- | ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
110	| `id`                | uuid                      | primary key                                                            |
111	| `program_id`        | uuid, FK -> `programs.id` | a class belongs to the program, independent of which sessions offer it |
112	| `name`              | string                    |                                                                        |
113	| `clubspot_class_id` | string, nullable, unique  | dedup key for #70                                                      |
114	
115	**session_classes** — which classes a session actually offers, i.e. the camp schedule itself. A
116	pure join, no fields of its own. Denormalized: Clubspot represents this as either an explicit
117	`CampSession.campClassesArray` or an `allClasses` flag meaning "every class in the program" — #70's
118	sync expands the `allClasses` case into one row per program class at sync time, so this table always
119	holds the actual explicit list and nothing downstream needs to special-case the flag. No Clubspot id
120	of its own — it's an array (or a flag) on `CampSession`, not a separate object — so #70 just
121	reconciles rows to match Clubspot's current state each sync (remove rows no longer present, add new
122	ones).
123	
124	| Field        | Type                      | Notes       |
125	| ------------ | ------------------------- | ----------- |
126	| `id`         | uuid                      | primary key |
127	| `session_id` | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id` |             |
128	| `class_id`   | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`  |             |
129	
130	**entry_caps** — capacity, matching Clubspot's `EntryCap` exactly: a cap on one class, either
131	overall (`session_id` null, applies across every session) or for one specific session.
132	
133	| Field                   | Type                                | Notes                                            |
134	| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
135	| `id`                    | uuid                                | primary key                                      |
136	| `class_id`              | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`            |                                                  |
137	| `session_id`            | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`, nullable | null = applies to this class across all sessions |
138	| `cap`                   | integer                             | the actual limit (Clubspot's own field name)     |
139	| `clubspot_entry_cap_id` | string, nullable, unique            | dedup key for #70                                |
140	
141	This — `programs` / `sessions` / `classes` / `session_classes` / `entry_caps` — is the camp
142	schedule: worth capturing accurately from #70's first sync rather than backfilling later, since the
143	website and the eventual financial-model app both need it, not just rosters/permissions.
144	
145	**registrations** — a participant's registration for one session + class (Clubspot's own term —
146	matched here rather than "enrollment"). This is deliberately at Clubspot's finest grain, its
147	`RegistrationCampSession` join ("Session Join Id" in the existing `ParticipantsReport`) rather than
148	its parent `Registration` object: a single Clubspot registration spanning multiple weeks/classes
149	becomes multiple rows here, one per session+class, matching what the current spreadsheet already
150	does. Billing/payment (Clubspot's `billing_registration`) stays out of scope, same as the rest of
151	the financial model.
152	
153	| Field                      | Type                                        | Notes                                                                                                                            |
154	| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
155	| `id`                       | uuid                                        | primary key                                                                                                                      |
156	| `person_id`                | uuid, FK -> `people.id`                     | the participant                                                                                                                  |
157	| `session_id`               | uuid, FK -> `sessions.id`                   |                                                                                                                                  |
158	| `class_id`                 | uuid, FK -> `classes.id`                    |                                                                                                                                  |
159	| `status`                   | enum (`confirmed`, `waitlist`, `cancelled`) | same vocabulary as #60; the _current_ status — see [Change tracking and provenance](#change-tracking-and-provenance) for history |
160	| `clubspot_registration_id` | string, nullable                            | groups rows from the same parent Clubspot registration (a multi-session signup); **not unique alone**                            |
161	| `clubspot_session_join_id` | string, nullable, unique                    | the true per-row dedup key for #70 (`RegistrationCampSession`'s own id)                                                          |
162	
163	### Change tracking and provenance
164	
165	Directus already does this: every API-driven create/update/delete is logged in `directus_activity`
166	(who, when, on what) with a paired `directus_revisions` row holding the full item snapshot and a
167	delta — for every collection, no opt-in needed. Architecture.md already assumed this
168	(`Audit — Directus activity log for data access/changes`), so there's no need for bespoke history
169	tables here, as long as #70 always writes through the Directus API (never raw SQL):
170	
171	- **Registration status** (waitlist → confirmed → cancelled) doesn't need its own event log — the
172	  revision history on a `registrations` row already shows every state it's been in and when Directus
173	  recorded each change. If Clubspot's own historical timestamps
174	  (`RegistrationCampSession.waitlist_updates`) matter and not just "when we noticed," #70's first
175	  import of a registration can replay each transition as its own sequential write so the revision
176	  _order_ matches reality — though the revision _timestamp_ is always "when Directus saw the write,"
177	  not the original Clubspot moment; a backfill can't inject history at an arbitrary past time.
178	- **Person contact-field changes** (a guardian's email changing between registrations two years
179	  apart) are the same story: the revision history on a `people` row already shows every value
180	  `email`/`phone`/`first_name`/`last_name` has held. Confirmed by looking at the live participants
181	  spreadsheet (the thing #70/#95 replace) — it's a fully-rebuilt-every-run flat snapshot with no
182	  timestamp or version on any row today, which is the actual gap here, and Directus's activity log
183	  closes it without any schema of our own.
184	
185	**What the activity log doesn't give us:** a revision is attributed to the Directus user who made
186	the write — for #70's automated updates that's always the sync's own service account, not _which
187	registration_ supplied a given value. No dedicated pointer for that here: `registrations.person_id`
188	already gives every registration a person touched, so "which one most recently supplied this email"
189	is a join against that plus the revision timestamps, not a separate FK on `people`.
190	
191	### Auth identity
192	
193	Auth info does not live on `people`. Directus already has its own identity table — `directus_users`
194	— with roles, policies, and OIDC `provider`/`external_identifier` fields for linking a Google login.
195	Reusing it instead of a homegrown field means:
196	
197	- `people.directus_user_id` is a nullable, unique FK to `directus_users.id`. Set only for people who
198	  have an actual login: staff now (provisioned directly by an admin); coach/guardian later, once
199	  #65's account-linking flow provisions or links a `directus_users` row on first OIDC login.
200	- Directus's own OIDC config does the email-matching (`provider` + `external_identifier` on
201	  `directus_users`). This schema has no identity/matching logic of its own — it only points `people`
202	  at the resulting user once one exists.
203	
204	### Permission model
205	
206	- **Administrator** — Directus's built-in full-access role.
207	- **Staff** — authenticates via Directus's native Google OIDC, restricted to Workspace accounts an
208	  admin has provisioned as Directus users. Full read/write on every collection above, including
209	  `medical_profiles`. The only role delivered end-to-end by #69/#92-#95.
210	- **Coach** — defined now so the schema doesn't need reshaping later, but has no way to log in yet
211	  (needs #65). KISS for now: any authenticated Directus user can read `sessions` / `registrations` /
212	  `people` roster fields (no `medical_profiles`) — scoping a coach to only their own sessions via
213	  `event_staff` is a follow-up, not built here.
214	- **Guardian** — same login caveat as Coach. Policy: read their own minors' `people` /
215	  `medical_profiles` / `registrations`, filtered through `contacts` where
216	  `relationship_type == 'guardian'`. This scoping isn't KISS'd away like the coach roster case above
217	  — it's the medical-data boundary the whole design doc exists to get right.
218	- **Emergency contacts get no role or login.** They're informational rows staff can see on a minor's
219	  record (`contacts` where `relationship_type == 'emergency_contact'`), not a portal audience.
220	
221	### Open questions for the applying slice (#95)
222	
223	- Exact Directus field types (`uuid` vs. Directus's integer PKs) for every collection above — pick
224	  whichever keeps the permission filters simplest when building the real schema snapshot.
225	- Whether `medical_profiles` needs field-level (not just collection-level) permissions before a
226	  Guardian role ever actually logs in.
227	- The actual person-dedup rule #70 will use (email match, most likely, with a manual merge path for
228	  the rest) — out of scope here, but the schema above assumes one exists.
229	- Whether contact-field provenance ever needs more than "join `registrations` on `person_id` and
230	  compare revision timestamps" — not built now; revisit if that join turns out too awkward for staff
231	  to actually use.
